hints: At a constant speed on a level road, acceleration is zero, so the engine driving force balances the total resistance force of the car and caravan combined.
Sum the resistances ($440 + 280 = 720\text{ N}$) and calculate the power using $P = F_D v$ with $v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Convert the resulting power from watts to kilowatts by dividing by $1000$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the total resistance on the level road at constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$F_D = R_{\text{car}} + R_{\text{caravan}} = 440 + 280 = 720\text{ N}$$

Calculate the power in watts and convert to kilowatts:
$$P = F_D \times v = 720 \times 30 = 21600\text{ W} = 21.6\text{ kW}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the relationship between mechanical power, driving force, and speed:
$$P = F_D v$$
Because the car and caravan travel along a straight horizontal road at a constant speed of $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the acceleration is zero ($a = 0$).

State Newton's second law for the combined system:
$$F_D - R_{\text{total}} = m_{\text{total}} a = 0$$
$$F_D = R_{\text{car}} + R_{\text{caravan}} = 440 + 280 = 720\text{ N}$$

Calculate the engine power in watts:
$$P = (720\text{ N})(30\text{ m s}^{-1}) = 21600\text{ W}$$

Convert the power into kilowatts as requested:
$$P = \frac{21600}{1000} = 21.6\text{ kW}$$
Thus the power developed by the engine of the car is $21.6\text{ kW}$.

hints: Find the new engine power ($21600 - 8000 = 13600\text{ W}$) and the corresponding new driving force at $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $F_D = \frac{13600}{30}$.
Apply Newton's second law to the whole system of total mass $2050\text{ kg}$ to calculate the instantaneous deceleration: $F_D - 720 = 2050a$.
Apply Newton's second law to the caravan ($800\text{ kg}$) alone, $T - 280 = 800a$, to determine the tow-bar tension T.
walkthrough:
Calculate the new driving force after power is decreased by $8\text{ kW}$ ($8000\text{ W}$):
$$P_{\text{new}} = 21600 - 8000 = 13600\text{ W}$$
$$F_D = \frac{13600}{30} = \frac{1360}{3} \approx 453.333\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the combined system of mass $1250 + 800 = 2050\text{ kg}$:
$$F_D - 720 = 2050a$$
$$453.333 - 720 = 2050a$$
$$-266.667 = 2050a \implies a = -\frac{266.667}{2050} \approx -0.130\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
$$\text{Deceleration} = 0.13\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the caravan ($m = 800\text{ kg}$, resistance $280\text{ N}$) to find tension $T$:
$$T - 280 = 800a = 800(-0.13008) = -104.065$$
$$T = 280 - 104.065 \approx 176\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Calculate the reduced engine power and the new forward driving force at the instant the power drops:
$$P_{\text{new}} = 21600\text{ W} - 8000\text{ W} = 13600\text{ W}$$
$$F_D = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{v} = \frac{13600}{30} = \frac{1360}{3} \approx 453.333\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law to the combined car and caravan system:
$$\sum F = m_{\text{total}} a$$
Total mass of the system:
$$m_{\text{total}} = 1250 + 800 = 2050\text{ kg}$$
Total resistance:
$$R_{\text{total}} = 440 + 280 = 720\text{ N}$$
Set up the equation of motion:
$$F_D - R_{\text{total}} = m_{\text{total}} a$$
$$453.333 - 720 = 2050a$$
$$-266.667 = 2050a$$
Divide both sides by $2050$:
$$a = -\frac{266.667}{2050} \approx -0.13008\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Therefore, the instantaneous deceleration is $0.13\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Consider the caravan alone to determine the tension $T$ in the tow-bar. Forces on the caravan:
- Forward pulling tension from tow-bar: $T$
- Backward resistance: $280\text{ N}$
Apply Newton's second law ($F_{\text{net}} = m_{\text{caravan}} a$):
$$T - 280 = 800a$$
Substitute $a = -0.13008\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$T - 280 = 800(-0.13008) = -104.064$$
Add $280$ to both sides:
$$T = 280 - 104.064 = 175.936\text{ N}$$
Rounding to three significant figures:
$$T = 176\text{ N}$$
Thus the tension in the tow-bar is $176\text{ N}$.

hints: When moving up the hill at constant speed, the driving force must balance the total resistance force plus the total component of weight parallel to the slope.
Calculate the total weight component down the hill: $W_{\parallel} = m_{\text{total}} g\sin\theta = 2050(10)(0.06) = 1230\text{ N}$.
Add the resistance $720\text{ N}$ to find the driving force $F_D = 1950\text{ N}$, then solve for $v$ using $P = F_D v$ with $P = 28080\text{ W}$ (or $28000\text{ W}$).
walkthrough:
Calculate the driving force required for the system to travel up the hill ($\sin\theta = 0.06$) at constant speed:
$$F_D = R_{\text{total}} + m_{\text{total}} g\sin\theta = 720 + 2050(10)(0.06)$$
$$F_D = 720 + 1230 = 1950\text{ N}$$

Use $P = F_D v$ with power $28000\text{ W}$ to solve for the constant speed $v$:
$$1950v = 28000$$
$$v = \frac{28000}{1950} = \frac{560}{39} \approx 14.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Identify the forces acting on the entire car and caravan system parallel to the hill:
- Forward driving force: $F_D$
- Resistances to motion: $R_{\text{total}} = 440 + 280 = 720\text{ N}$
- Downward component of total weight: $W_{\parallel} = m_{\text{total}} g\sin\theta$

Calculate the component of total weight down the slope:
$$W_{\parallel} = (1250 + 800)(10)(0.06) = 2050(10)(0.06) = 1230\text{ N}$$

State Newton's second law for the system moving at constant speed ($a = 0$):
$$F_D - R_{\text{total}} - W_{\parallel} = 0$$
$$F_D = 720 + 1230 = 1950\text{ N}$$

Use the power equation $P = F_D v$ to determine the speed:
$$P = F_D v$$
$$28000 = 1950 v$$
Divide both sides by $1950$:
$$v = \frac{28000}{1950} = \frac{560}{39} \approx 14.359\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Rounding to three significant figures gives:
$$v = 14.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Thus the constant speed of the car and caravan is $14.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

hints: In one minute ($t = 60\text{ s}$), calculate the distance travelled up the hill using $d = vt$ with your speed from part (b)(i).
Calculate the vertical height gained by the caravan using $h = d\sin\theta = d(0.06)$.
Calculate the increase in potential energy of the caravan alone ($m = 800\text{ kg}$) using $\Delta E_p = mgh$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the distance travelled up the incline in $60\text{ s}$:
$$d = v \times 60 = 14.359 \times 60 \approx 861.54\text{ m}$$

Calculate the vertical height gained:
$$h = d\sin\theta = 861.54 \times 0.06 \approx 51.692\text{ m}$$

Calculate the potential energy increase for the $800\text{ kg}$ caravan:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh = 800(10)(51.692) \approx 413538\text{ J} \approx 414000\text{ J}\text{ (or }414\text{ kJ)}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the formula for gravitational potential energy increase:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh$$
where $m$ is the mass of the caravan, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $h$ is the vertical height gained in one minute ($60\text{ s}$).

Calculate the distance $d$ travelled along the inclined road in $60\text{ s}$ using the exact speed $v = \frac{560}{39}\text{ m s}^{-1}$ from part (b)(i):
$$d = v t = \left(\frac{560}{39}\right)(60) = \frac{33600}{39} = \frac{11200}{13} \approx 861.538\text{ m}$$

Calculate the vertical height gained $h$ using $\sin\theta = 0.06$:
$$h = d\sin\theta = \left(\frac{11200}{13}\right)(0.06) = \frac{672}{13} \approx 51.6923\text{ m}$$

Substitute the values into the potential energy equation for the caravan ($m = 800\text{ kg}$):
$$\Delta E_p = (800\text{ kg})(10\text{ m s}^{-2})\left(\frac{672}{13}\text{ m}\right) = 8000 \times \frac{672}{13} = \frac{5376000}{13} \approx 413538\text{ J}$$

Round to three significant figures:
$$\Delta E_p = 414000\text{ J} = 414\text{ kJ}$$
Thus the increase in potential energy of the caravan in one minute is $414000\text{ J}$ (or $414\text{ kJ}$).
